scope: Read-only inspection of four pinned source/config files. This report records source implications, not a Clean evaluation, security experiment or deployed vulnerability.

source.revision_binding_scope: Revision taken from the existing source-screen provenance; no new network or hash verification.

findings.finding: osrp_vector uses CCEPlanner, use_cost=False and cost_limit=0.0. CCE geometry converts each of eight reconstructed hazard distances to a 0/1 indicator and sums them. Its nonnegative trajectory sum can never satisfy the strict test traj_cost < 0.0, so num_safe_traj is zero and the planner ranks all candidates by negative geometric cost.
findings.formula: c_t = sum_{j=1..8} 1[||reconstructed_hazard_{t,j}|| <= 0.25]; C_i = sum_{t=0..H} c_{t,i}; safe_count = sum_i 1[C_i < 0] = 0
findings.temporal_scope: WorldModel.imagine prepends the current state. The CCE geometry branch evaluates and sums H+1 states including that start state, without the standard OSRP factor 1000/H.
limits: This does not imply every trajectory is physically unsafe. Even zero predicted geometric cost fails this strict zero threshold.
Zero-cost ties are handled by top_k over negative cost, with no reward tie-break in this branch.

CCEPlanner.cost_from_recon counts hazards; the separate WorldModel.cost_from_recon and PID helper collapse to a binary indicator. Those helpers must not be substituted when describing CCE Vector behavior.
This is a source/configuration consequence, not a measured task failure or attack.

source_locations.why: H imagined transitions plus prepended initial state

findings.finding: Each candidate gets one stochastic RSSM trajectory in each optimization round, not an ensemble of repeated futures for a fixed candidate. The cost head returns a distribution mean per future latent; CCE sums those H values and multiplies by 1000/H. If fewer than 50 candidates meet the strict cost limit, the whole batch is ranked by negative cost; otherwise the safe-index reward branch is used.
findings.formula: C_i = (1000/H) * sum_{t=1..H} mean(cost_head(z_{t,i})); safe_count = sum_i 1[C_i < cost_limit]
findings.cost_head_scope: The configured symlog_disc head has signed support (-20, 20 in transformed coordinates); source does not constrain its predicted mean to be nonnegative. The Vector nonnegativity argument therefore does not apply to standard OSRP.
limits: The count is over distinct candidate trajectories, not repeated success/safety observations for one candidate and not a chance-constraint confidence certificate.
The cost gate uses raw predicted cost means, not cost_ret, a terminal cost critic value, or a continuation-weighted sum.
No sampling-law, calibration, checkpoint quality or real task capability has been tested by this review.

source_locations.why: Cost distribution and inherited planner defaults
Single candidate batch, H-step cost aggregation and all-batch gate
CostVFunction.score returns raw cost separately from cost return
One stochastic RSSM sample per batch row per transition

findings.finding: The reward branch calls jnp.nonzero(mask, size=mask.size) without fill_value, whose default zero-index padding produces a fixed-size list containing repeated candidate 0 when safe_count < N. Those entries are subsequently eligible for top_k.
findings.trigger_scope: The reward branch is selected when safe_count >= num_elites. Thus padding matters when num_elites <= safe_count < N. If candidate 0 is unsafe, padding can reintroduce it; if it is safe, repeated copies can still change elite multiplicities and the mean. Actual selection depends on its score and ties.
limits: When all N candidates are safe there is no padding; below the elite count the cost-only branch is used.
This review did not execute JAX or observe a real candidate bank, so it does not establish occurrence or physical harm in a trained model.
No externally controllable writer or distinct adversarial mechanism has been demonstrated.

findings.finding: CCE computes an elite action-sequence mean, applies configured momentum against the previous mean, and returns the first action of that updated mean. It does not re-run dynamics or cost validation on the final mean before returning it. The result is generally not an individual scored candidate, although coincidence is possible.
findings.formula: mu_new = momentum * mu_old + (1 - momentum) * mean(elite_sequences); executed_action = mu_new[0]; inherited momentum = 0.1
limits: Safe scored elites do not by themselves certify the returned mean in a nonlinear environment.
The source gap does not prove that the returned mean is unsafe or that any real task suffers.
A hypothetical safety analysis must follow the returned mean, not attribute the outcome of one elite candidate to the executed action.

source_locations.why: Elite mean, smoothing and direct return

native_decision_consumption.finding: Agent constructs CCEPlanner from expl_behavior and explicitly selects expl_outs in eval mode for CCEPlanner. It also uses those outputs in train/explore modes and retains the returned action in recurrent state. Thus the reviewed planner output is on the native action path, not merely a diagnostic.

source_locations.why: Planner outputs selected by policy mode

native_decision_consumption.boundary: No environment execution, task success, real constraint violation or deployed external intervention is established by this source path.

decision.source_conclusions: The four stated source facts are supported with the Vector/standard-OSRP distinctions above.
decision.note: These implementation and aggregation facts do not alone justify a trained-model safety claim or a new experiment.
